scope: Only layout, readability, actual clipping or overlap, and visible missing-media symptoms within the eight listed native-pixel coverage regions. No semantic, SCI, ZHEN, answer, modern-figure, or whole-product re-review.

findings.observation: The covered right-hand circuit portion renders with clear wires, junctions, capacitor strokes and headphone outlines. The Headphones label is fully readable within this region; no label-wire overlap, missing-image placeholder or blank media failure is visible.

The diode label begins with only its suffix in this horizontal slice, and leftward wires meet the slice boundary. This is the declared native content range 310..620 of a 640px figure, not evidence that the product clipped or lost the full label. Uncovered content is not granted a visual PASS here.

The page title, question numbers, first question and options, and the covered second-question text are readable, with stable left gutters, usable line spacing and no text-radio or text-checkbox overlap. Muted empty choice controls are legitimate readonly/disabled presentation, not a display failure.
The last second-question option continues below the 1536px tile boundary; this is a tile cut rather than evidence of product text clipping.

The covered question 3 prose, superscripted scientific notation, capacitance and wavelength option lines are legible and fit the text column without overlap. The visible left-hand circuit portion renders, with antenna, coil, variable-capacitor, ground and labels separated.

A continuation fragment at the top and option continuation at the bottom are tile boundaries. The circuit reaches the right edge of its horizontal figure viewport; this slice does not establish clipping of the full scrolling figure, whose right-hand covered portion is observed separately in this batch.

The remaining question 3 option, question 4 text, hatted vectors and cross-product formula are readable with no text collision. The covered antenna/building illustration has visible linework and fills, not a missing or broken image. The covered first option stays separated from the illustration.

The top and bottom text continuations follow fullpage tile cuts. The illustration's rightward elements end at the horizontal viewport boundary; no conclusion about unseen rightward figure content is substituted for visual observation.

Question 4 options and question 5 prose/formulas remain readable. Hats, vector symbols, subscripts and square-root expressions are visible; the formula lines do not overlap preceding or following prose or extend outside the covered text column. The next illustration starts below the question with clear separation.

The leading option continuation and lower illustration cutoff are tile boundaries, while the illustration reaches its horizontal viewport edge. These partial coverage boundaries are not reported as product defects.

The lower illustration strokes are visible above the question 5 options. All covered options have readable prose and vector expressions with adequate line spacing and clear separation from the controls. Question 6 begins cleanly after its divider, with readable stem and covered options.
The illustration continuation at the top and question 6 option continuation at the bottom are declared tile boundaries, not overlap or evidence of missing document content.

The final question 6 option wraps into three readable lines with its checkbox in the gutter. Its last line and the lower whitespace are visible, without bottom truncation or overlap. The tiny text fragment at the tile's upper edge is the preceding tile continuation.

The covered right-hand circuit portion in the choices surface is rendered with clear junctions, capacitor lines, headphone circles and a readable Headphones label. No wire-label collision, missing-media placeholder or visually broken raster is visible.

The left-boundary diode-label suffix and incoming wires are expected within the specified 310..620 native-content slice. This was opened as its own listed choices-surface image, not as a reopen of the exercises-surface image; hidden parts beyond the region are not visually certified.
